sara_custeng: Hey team — hitting a reproducible case where SSE streams from /v1/streams/generate stop with an incomplete JSON payload. The last data event ends with a trailing comma and there is no finish_reason or final [DONE] event, so our client JSON.parse fails and we treat it as a hard failure. Repro steps + curl below.

sara_custeng: ```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-13b-v2 \
  -d '{"prompt":"<very long prompt>","max_tokens":4096}'
```

miguel: Can you paste the raw tail of the SSE you received (exact bytes if possible)? Also send the X-Request-ID header from the response.

sara_custeng: Request-ID: 0xabc123def. Raw tail (we saved the stream to a file and opened in hex/text):

sara_custeng: ```
data: {"id":"tok-1","delta":"...chunk A"}
data: {"id":"tok-1","delta":"...chunk B"}
data: {"id":"tok-1","delta":"final part",}
<socket closed by peer>
```

sara_custeng: Note the trailing comma after the final object and then the TCP FIN. No "data: [DONE]", no finish_reason.

arya: Thanks — can you confirm: are you doing any automatic auth token rotation mid-generation? Any client-side reconnect/resume logic using Last-Event-ID or custom resume headers?

sara_custeng: We rotate short-lived tokens via our proxy every ~60s. This particular generation lasted ~90s so token rotation happened mid-stream. Our client does a reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` set to the last event id it got. We also attach our own header `X-Resume-Cursor` with the byte offset.

arya: That helps. We pulled the upstream proxy logs for 0xabc123def:

arya: ```
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] auth-proxy: rotated token for client svc-42
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] ingress: stream 0xabc123def upstream->redwood: RST_STREAM (code=2)
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] ingress: connection closed while flushing chunked buffer
```

infra_oncall: We have an outstanding edge case where a reconnect flow that attempts to resume a partially flushed event can end up with the last event left without the terminating newline. In combination with a trailing-comma in the serialized delta object this yields an invalid JSON payload when the client concatenates chunks. Ticket SRE-1982 tracks a fix.

miguel: Short-term mitigations for your side: 1) avoid rotating tokens mid-generation if possible, 2) make the client streaming parser tolerant to a trailing comma (or buffer until connection close + re-validate), 3) if you can send a small keepalive to prevent token refresh during long generations.

miguel: From platform side we reproduced this in staging. Root cause: when the upstream RST_STREAM races with the server flush path, the final '\n' delimiter for the SSE event may be dropped. When the JSON emitter also includes a trailing comma (e.g., generator emitted an empty field), the concatenation yields '\",}' which is invalid.

arya: We opened PR #4567 that ensures the SSE emitter always writes an explicit final sentinel event before initiating token refresh, and makes the flush path idempotent. Staging deploy of pr/4567 is running now.

ci-bot: Deployment: pr/4567 -> staging succeeded (build 6789) :white_check_mark:

miguel: Can you test against staging (we added an environment URL below) and share whether you still see truncated JSON? If it passes, we'll roll to prod.

sara_custeng: Testing now against https://staging.api.redwood.ai — will report back in ~15m. Thanks for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

aria (typo correction): (not a participant)

aria: (ignore)

sara_custeng: Follow-up: staging looks good, the final event and finish_reason are delivered when we re-run the same long prompt. We'll keep an eye on prod after you roll.

miguel: Great — escalation complete. We'll schedule prod rollout and link the prod release to SRE-1982. Will also add a short doc about token-rotation best practices for streaming clients.

infra_oncall: Escalation JIRA: SRE-1982. Prod rollout target: 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC (post-maintenance window).

sara_custeng: Thanks all. We'll reopen if anything else crops up.
